deep.reconstruction:
Purpose: Gauss reads the hypergeometric equation for the complete elliptic integral, rewritten with the nome z = q as independent variable, as a nonlinear differential system for the theta-nullwerte. Modern notation used below: θ3 = 1+2z+2z^4+…, θ4 = 1−2z+2z^4−…, θ2 = 2z^{1/4}+2z^{9/4}+…, D = z d/dz, ' = d/dz, and Gauss's ϖ stands for π.

(1) The ODE. 0 = ¼P − (1−2x)P_x − x(1−x)P_xx is Gauss's line, the extra term (x−xx)dP·d²x/dx³ being included because dx is not assumed constant. This is the hypergeometric equation x(1−x)P'' + (1−2x)P' − P/4 = 0, with c=1, a=b=½.

(2) Solutions. P = F(½,½;1;x) = 1 + ¼x + (1·9)/(4·16)x² + … = (2/π)K(k), with x = k². Q = P(1−x) = (2/π)K'.

(3) Wronskian. Q dP − P dQ = dx/(π x(1−x)). The form C/(x(1−x)) follows from Abel's formula; the constant 1/π is equivalent to Legendre's relation.

(4) Theta inversion, stated without proof.
- P = θ3(z)².
- x = θ2⁴/θ3⁴, i.e. x = (2z^{1/4}+2z^{9/4}+…)⁴/P².
- z = exp(−πQ/P) = exp(−πK'/K), the nome. Equivalently −Q = P log z/π.

(5) Change of variable [my step]. Differentiating log z gives dz/z = π(Q dP − P dQ)/P². Using (3), P² dz/z = dx/(x(1−x)), which is Gauss's line.

(6) Second differential. With dz constant: d²x/(x−xx) − dx²(1−2x)/(x−xx)² = 2P dP dz/z − P² dz²/z².

(7) The ODE in z [my check]. Insert (6) into (1); equivalently note x(1−x)P_x = DP/P². This gives P·D²P − 2(DP)² = ¼P⁶x(1−x), i.e. 0 = ¼P⁶(x−xx) + 2z²P'² − zPP' − z²PP''.

(8) Reciprocal. With P = 1/T the quadratic terms cancel: D²T = −¼T⁻³x(1−x), i.e. 0 = ¼T⁻³(x−xx) + z²T'' + zT'.

(9) Introduce U = θ4^{−2}. Then 1−x = T²/U² (Jacobi's identity θ3⁴ = θ2⁴ + θ4⁴), so x(1−x) = T²(U²−T²)/U⁴. This yields the coupled system:
- 0 = ¼(U²−T²)/(U⁴T) + D²T;
- 0 = ¼(U²−T²)/(UT⁴) − D²U.
The second follows from the first under z→−z, which swaps T and U and leaves D invariant.

(10) Right column: first integral. Now P = θ3², Q = θ4², x = 1 − Q²/P². From (5) one gets z(QP' − PQ') = ½PQ(P²−Q²); Gauss writes ¼. In T,U form the correct statement is z(TU' − UT') = ½(U/T − T/U); Gauss writes ¼(U/T − T/U) = z(UT' − TU').

(11) Differentiation. Differentiating gives z·d/dz[...] = z(UT'−TU') + z²(UT''−TU''). The correct combination of the two second-order equations is U·D²T − T·D²U = −¼(U⁴−T⁴)/(T³U³). Gauss gets (U²−T²)² in the numerator because of a sign slip. The next page has the correct 4UT'' − 4TU'' + (U⁴−T⁴)/(T³U³) = 0, together with the first integral 2(TU'−UT')² = ½(T²/U² + U²/T²) − 1.

(12) Series check of (8).
- T = θ3^{−2} = 1 − 4z + 12z² − 32z³ + 76z⁴.
- zT' = −4z + 24z² − 96z³ + 304z⁴.
- z²T'' = 24z² − 192z³ + 912z⁴.
- D²T = −4z + 48z² − 288z³ + 1216z⁴ = −4z(1 − 12z + 72z² − 304z³).
- The other side: ¼T⁻³x(1−x) = ¼θ2⁴θ4⁴/θ3² = 4z(1+z²+…)⁴·T/U². Here (1+z²)⁴ = 1 + 4z² + 6z⁴, T/U² = θ4⁴/θ3² = 1 − 12z + 68z² − 256z³, and U² = θ4^{−4} = 1 + 8z + 40z².
- (1+4z²)(1−12z+68z²−256z³) = 1 − 12z + 72z² − 304z³, so the check succeeds.

The marginal scribbles (6ppp't', p²t'', 3p⁵tt') anticipate the next page's substitution T = p^{−2}. That page leads toward a third-order nonlinear ODE for θ3.
errors: The constant written ϖ must be π (ordinary circle constant) for P=θ3², z=e^{-ϖQ/P} and QdP−PdQ=dx/(ϖ x(1−x)) to be consistent; not the lemniscate ϖ=2.622…

Right column: z(QP'−PQ') = ½ PQ(P²−Q²), not ¼; correspondingly z(TU'−UT') = ½(U/T − T/U), whereas Gauss writes ¼(U/T−T/U) = z(UT'−TU'), wrong in both factor and sign. The intermediate line (UU−TT)/(U³T³)=zT'/(UTT)−zU'/(TUU) also drops the factor and has the sign reversed.

Derivative of ¼(U/T−T/U) is ¼(TU'−UT')(1/T²+1/U²), not (1/T²−1/U²); this sign slip makes Gauss get (UU−TT)²/(4T³U³) instead of the correct (U⁴−T⁴)/(4T³U³) (with sign: U D²T − T D²U = −¼(U⁴−T⁴)/(T³U³)). Corrected on the next page.
The step 'al.' (substituting (6) into (1)) is written in garbled, unjustified form, but its result 0 = ¼P⁶(x−xx)+2z²P'²−zPP'−z²PP'' is correct.
Theta-inversion formulas (P=θ3², x=θ2⁴/θ3⁴, z=e^{−πK'/K}) are asserted without proof (known results, consistent with his other Nachlass).

results.what: Hypergeometric ODE for F(1/2,1/2;1;x) with the two solutions P(x), P(1−x) and Wronskian 1/(π x(1−x))
results.modern_name: Picard–Fuchs / hypergeometric equation for K(k); Legendre relation in Wronskian form
Theta-function inversion of the elliptic modulus (nome)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi 1829 (Fundamenta Nova); Gauss in Nachlass (AGM/theta, c.1800–1818)

results.what: Rewriting the K-equation with the nome as variable: P·D²P − 2(DP)² = ¼P⁶x(1−x), and for T=θ3^{-2}: D²T = −¼T^{-3}x(1−x)
results.modern_name: Differential equation satisfied by theta-nullwerte (modular-form ODE)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi 1847/48 (Crelle 36, 'Über die Differentialgleichung, welcher die Reihen 1±2q+2q⁴+… Genüge leisten')

results.what: Coupled nonlinear system for T=θ3^{-2}, U=θ4^{-2}: D²T = −¼(U²−T²)/(U⁴T), D²U = ¼(U²−T²)/(UT⁴), with first integral z(TU'−UT') = ½(U/T−T/U)
results.modern_name: Nonlinear ODE system for theta constants (cf. Jacobi's third-order equation, Halphen/Darboux-type systems)

results.what: Power-series verification of the T-equation using θ2⁴ = 16z(1+z²+…)⁴ and θ4⁴/θ3² expansions

deep.surprise_reason: The theta/AGM inversion is well known to be Gauss's. But deriving a nonlinear differential equation for the theta constants, by turning the nome into the independent variable of the K-equation (with a first integral and, on the next page, a third-order equation for θ3), anticipates Jacobi's 1847 paper. I am not certain the Werke edition highlights this. It is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major new result, and the page itself still contains uncorrected slips.

checkable.asserts: Correct first integral z(TU'−UT') = ½(U/T−T/U) (Gauss's ¼ and sign on this page are wrong)
Jacobi identity θ3⁴ = θ4⁴ + θ2⁴, so x = θ2⁴/θ3⁴ = 1 − T²/U²
P = F(1/2,1/2;1;x) satisfies the page's ODE

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x'); P=2/pi*elliptic_k(x); Q=2/pi*elliptic_k(1-x); N(Q*diff(P,x)-P*diff(Q,x)-1/(pi*x*(1-x)).subs(x,Rational(3,10)) if False else (Q*diff(P,x)-P*diff(Q,x)-1/(pi*x*(1-x))).subs(x,Rational(3,10)))
checkable.asserts: Wronskian Q P' − P Q' = 1/(π x(1−x)) with ϖ = π (numerically ≈ 0)

Right column final bracket: first entry is zUT' (not zU'T'), i.e. {zUT' + zzUT'' − zTU' − zzTU''}.
The line beginning 'al.' has a garbled factor '(∂x∂)²/(∂x)³'; it represents substituting the expression for d²x into the term (x−xx)dP·d²x/dx³ of the original ODE.
In '0=¼T^{-3}(x−xx)…' there is a struck-out exponent digit before −3; the intended exponent is −3.
'1/(P³Q)' beside '¼PPdz/z = QdP−PdQ' is a marginal multiplier note, not part of the equation.
Line '0=¼(UU−TT)/(U⁴T)' – the denominator in the image shows U⁴ over a struck/overwritten T; reads U⁴T.
Bottom line '1+8 +40' is the series U² = θ4^{-4} = 1+8z+40z²+…
